payload.alternatives: Keep the PHP split as a generated read-only mirror: one more public repository and a token to keep, for no user-facing gain; Study first with a throwaway Packagist package: delays the move; Delete the split repositories: lock files that download the old zips from them would break, archiving keeps them
payload.rationale: Every issue, pull request and release already happened here; the split repositories only mirrored packages/php and packages/js through a personal access token. Packagist.org needs composer.json at the repository root (packagist.org/about; blog.packagist.com/installing-composer-packages-from-monorepos), so the root holds one for the single PHP package, with autoload into packages/php/src and export-ignore so the archive Composer downloads holds only the PHP package; a CI job fails when it drifts from packages/php/composer.json. The npm metadata already named this repository.
payload.title: PHP and JS are published from this repository alone: Packagist reads the root composer.json, npm publishes packages/js at its js-v tag, and the split repositories are archived after a backup

payload.alternatives: Keep php-v tags: Packagist ignores them; Let the old versions go: published versions would disappear from Packagist and lock files would point at nothing
payload.rationale: Packagist reads only X.Y.Z or vX.Y.Z tags. The old tags point at commits that already have composer.json at their root, so bringing them in keeps every published version on the same commit, the reference users' lock files hold; none of those names exists here. JS keeps its js-v tags.
payload.title: PHP releases are tagged vX.Y.Z, and the split repository's old v tags are brought into this repository under the same names before Packagist is pointed here

payload.alternatives: bootstrap-sha: applies only when no release exists; Keep the component in the tag: Packagist would not read it
payload.rationale: With the tag component off, release-please 17.6.0 (the version the pinned action carries) no longer finds the php-v releases and would put the whole history in the next changelog (95 commits measured by a dry run); last-release-sha bounds it, and the next version comes from the manifest.
payload.title: release-please walks PHP history only back to last-release-sha until the first vX PHP release, and the key is removed after that release, never before
